title: Diagnosing Parkinson's Disease
content: Parkinson's disease is diagnosed clinically using a person's medical history, symptoms and physical or neurological examination. There is no single laboratory test or scan that conclusively confirms Parkinson's disease. Healthcare professionals evaluate patterns of movement symptoms and other clinical findings. Tests such as brain imaging or blood tests may sometimes be used to help rule out other possible causes or support clinical assessment. Because early symptoms can be mild and can overlap with other conditions, diagnosis may require specialist evaluation. A screening result, tremor, voice change, gait abnormality or questionnaire result alone should therefore never be presented as confirmation that a person has Parkinson's disease.
